correctness.rationale: Condition on full previous preferences and assignments at stage t: exactly k_t=n−t+1 schools remain and exactly r_t earlier assigned schools went to lower-priority pupils. The current student uniformly ranks their union, so justified envy iff her best therein is among r_t schools, with conditional probability r_t/(k_t+r_t), constant over history. Iterated conditioning proves joint Bernoulli independence and the product generating function. For a priority-inverted adjacent pair at t,t+1, direct rational algebra gives strict increase of its zero-envy probability and double-claimant difference Δ2=r[s−(k−1+r)]/[(k+s)(k+r)(k−1+r)]. For n≤4, r≥1 and s>k−1+r cannot coexist; a stochastic improvement of the changed two-variable sum survives convolution by unchanged independent indicators. The n=5 orders (2,3,5,4,1) and (2,3,5,1,4) yield tails P(Z≥1):13/15→4/5 and P(Z≥2):4/15→3/10. Independent exact rational comparisons over all 283 priority-correcting adjacent swaps in n≤5 and explicit witness fractions corroborate; the universal proof is conditional-uniformity, not finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: Hamdan 2026 studies the same serial mechanism and priority fairness and extends Kemeny expected counts of pairwise blocking cases to independent preferences, but expected number of blocking pairs is not the distribution of the number of distinct students with any justified envy. The inspected full text does not establish joint Bernoulli factorization or sharp five-agent upper-tail reversal. Abdulkadiroğlu et al. and Ortega–Klein compare mechanism fairness and expected student envy with differing priority models. Qualified PASS; an indexed or implicit formula in older distributional matching studies remains possible.
residual_risks: Uniform independently drawn complete rankings and ex ante fixed order are essential; correlated preferences or school-specific priorities need not factorize.
A general probability-of-blocking-student theorem may entail the factorization under another notation.
The result counts students with at least one claim, not pairs of envy claims.

value.rationale: A policymaker may care about the risk of two or more distinct justified-envy claimants, not only expected blocking pairs or probability of any envy. The exact Poisson-binomial law and minimal five-student exception show an intuitively priority-improving swap can worsen a nontrivial tail risk while improving the envy-free probability. This is a motivated distributional fairness boundary.

final_claim: Under serial dictatorship with fixed common school priority and independently uniform student preference rankings, student justified-envy indicators are jointly independent Bernoulli with p_t=r_t/(n−t+1+r_t). Adjacent priority correction always raises P(no envy) and stochastically improves the envy count through n=4, but n=5 is first to reverse the two-claimant upper tail.
